verdict.rationale: Jitsu documents its own connector syncs that pull data into the warehouse from third-party sources. These are Airbyte-compatible connectors covering 300+ sources such as Google Analytics and Stripe, and they run as scheduled Kubernetes CronJobs with failure and recovery alerts. It can also receive data forwarded from Segment via a webhook. A community user reports that Jitsu covers most of the ad sources they care about but has a higher setup bar than Segment, which is a caveat on ease of use rather than a contradiction. Missing for 10: detailed per-connector documentation (configuration, sync modes, incremental behavior) and independent hands-on corroboration of connector syncs working.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I can pull customer data in from third-party cloud apps and feeds — not just my own instrumented apps

citations.quote: Connector syncs — pull data *into* your warehouse from third-party sources (Airbyte-compatible connectors).
offering seamless connections to over 300+ data sources including giants like Google Analytics, Stripe, and Postgres.
Now you can use Jitsu to pull data from your favorite SaaS apps, databases and custom sources.
connector syncs run as Kubernetes CronJobs
Set up a webhook destination in Segment and send data to Jitsu and get it into your DB in real-time.
